Implements
[programming spec 0003](../../specs/features/002-programming/specs/0003-playback-ordering.md).
Source and executable tests are canonical after implementation.

## Reconnaissance

Collection-sourced blocks play `chronological` (saved membership position) or
`random` (seeded selection index). Progress is one row per channel and
collection with one column per mode. Each schedule entry records the
collection, mode, and position or index it consumed, and regeneration rewinds
progress to the earliest deleted entry. Spec 0001 already stores every fact
the new orders need, with the owner's corrections applied in one place.

Accepted ADRs: [ADR 0009](../../adrs/0009-programming-blocks.md), amended on
2026-10-13, owns identity-based continuation and per-mode progress.
[ADR 0003](../../adrs/0003-materialized-schedule-entries.md) protects the
airing entry; every regeneration here goes through `applyInputChange`.
[ADR 0006](../../adrs/0006-media-roots-and-collections.md) keeps saved
membership the only stored order. [ADR 0010](../../adrs/0010-source-layout.md)
places the files. Ordering policy lives in kraziBrain; the server only
assembles effective facts. Glossary terms used: **Playback mode**, **Playback
progress**, **Programming block**, **Schedule entry**, **Regeneration**,
**Regeneration boundary**, **Correction**, **Extra**, **Window dialog**.

### Design Decisions This Plan Makes

The spec leaves these to implementation; each ticket below follows them.
Change them here before the ticket lands, not inside it.

| Decision                  | Choice                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Progress rows             | `channel_collection_progress` becomes one row per `(channel_id, media_collection_id, playback_mode)` with nullable `last_media_item_id` and `last_position` (ordered modes), `next_selection_index` (random), and nullable `reset_sequence_number`. `last_media_item_id` is set null when purge deletes the item, which falls back to the position.          |
| Resume rule               | Identity in the new order → the position after it. Identity absent, position known → `last_position` modulo the member count. Neither → position `0`. Walk forward from there skipping unschedulable members, as `selectChronological` does today.                                                                                                           |
| Migration                 | Each existing row splits into a `chronological` and a `random` row. A `next_chronological_position` of `N > 0` becomes `last_position = (N - 1) % count` with the member at that place in saved order as the identity, so the next pick is unchanged. An empty collection keeps `last_position = N` with no identity. `N = 0` leaves both null.              |
| Mode constraint           | Migration `019` (ORD-002) rebuilds `programming_blocks` and `schedule_entries` so their `playback_mode` CHECK allows all four spec modes at once; requests still accept only `PLAYBACK_MODES`. The rebuild turns foreign-key enforcement off around one transaction, runs `foreign_key_check`, and turns it back on, so entries keep their block references. |
| Restoration               | For each collection and mode the deleted entries used, progress becomes the latest kept entry of that channel, collection, and mode (its media item and position). Kept entries before `reset_sequence_number` are ignored. With none left, progress is the beginning. Random keeps today's rewind to the earliest deleted index.                            |
| Ordering facts            | `ScheduleMedia` gains `savedPosition`, `seriesKey`, `seasonNumber`, `episodeNumber`, and `releaseDate`, built from `effectiveMetadata` and `effectiveContentIdentity`. Extras and unmatched items carry nulls and sort as unresolved.                                                                                                                        |
| Series key                | Built in kraziBrain: `tmdb:<id>` when the effective TMDB series ID exists, else `name:<name>` lowercased with whitespace trimmed and collapsed. Series sort by key, so the order is stable but not alphabetical by title; the preview shows the grouping.                                                                                                    |
| Duplicates                | Two members with the same series key, season, and episode. Flagged in the preview only; both stay selectable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Ordering-change detection | Ordered progress rows store `order_fingerprint`, a hash of the ordered member IDs the last generation used. The maintenance pass recomputes it for every block in `episode` or `release` mode and regenerates the channels whose fingerprint changed, with reason `ordering_changed`. Equal fingerprints do nothing.                                         |
| Preview                   | `GET /channels/:id/programming-blocks/:blockId/preview?playbackMode=` returns the ordered view with flags and the block's next ten upcoming schedule entries. Passing a mode previews it before saving; upcoming entries are shown only for the saved mode.                                                                                                  |
| Reset                     | `POST /channels/:id/programming-blocks/:blockId/progress-reset` resets that block's channel, collection, and saved mode, records `reset_sequence_number`, and regenerates through `applyInputChange` with reason `progress_reset`. Confirmed in a **Window dialog**.                                                                                         |

**Sequencing note**: ORD-001 comes first. ORD-002 needs ORD-001. ORD-003 and
ORD-004 each need ORD-002. ORD-005 needs ORD-002. ORD-006 needs ORD-004.

### ORD-001: Continue collection order by identity, with per-mode progress

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-14. Ordered selection resumes after the last selected
item, falling back to its position; progress is one row per channel,
collection, and mode, and migration 018 preserves every existing next pick.
`reset_sequence_number` is stored but unused until ORD-006.

**Goal**: Collection order resumes after the last item it played when the
collection is reordered or changed, and each mode keeps its own progress row.

**Scope**:

- Migration `018` reshapes `channel_collection_progress` as decided above,
  preserving every existing channel's next pick.
- `PlaybackProgress` becomes per mode. Ordered selection applies the resume
  rule. `RestorableEntry` carries `mediaItemId`; restoration follows the
  restoration decision.
- `loadProgress`, `upsertProgress`, and `restoreDeletedProgress` read and
  write per-mode rows.

**Out of scope**: New modes; the preview; reset.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer. Write the kraziBrain selection and restoration
  tests first (tdd skill).
- `reset_sequence_number` is added now and stays null until ORD-006.

**Verification**:

- kraziBrain tests: unchanged order resumes at the next position; an insert
  before the last item, a reorder, and removal of the last item each resume
  as the rule says; unschedulable members are skipped; the order loops.
- Restoration test: deleting future entries restores the latest kept entry;
  chunked generation, a restart, and regeneration produce identical entries.
- Migration test: rows at `N = 0`, mid-collection, and after a wrap pick the
  same next item as before.
- Existing schedule, playout, and Plex acceptance suites pass unchanged.

**Docs impact**: None.

### ORD-002: Play a collection in episode order

**Goal**: A block can play its collection by series, season, and episode
while another channel plays the same collection in saved order.

**Scope**:

- Add `episode` to `PLAYBACK_MODES`.
- `loadScheduleSource` selects members with `METADATA_COLUMNS` and builds the
  ordering facts.
- `ordered-view.ts` in kraziBrain orders members for a mode: series key,
  season (`0` first), first episode, then unresolved members in saved order;
  ties by saved position, then media item ID.
- The programming editor offers Collection order, Episode order, and Random,
  with a one-line explanation under the select.

**Out of scope**: Release order; the preview; regeneration on metadata change.

**Blocking dependencies**: ORD-001.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer; the editor change is a thin UI slice.
- A multi-episode file sorts at `episodeNumber` and airs once; ordering never
  reads `lastEpisodeNumber`.
- Saved membership rows are never written.

**Verification**:

- kraziBrain tests: mixed series group by key; a corrected series name groups
  by name; season zero first; multi-episode at its first episode; unresolved
  and extra members last in saved order; ties stable.
- Route test: one collection airs in saved order on one channel and episode
  order on another; saved positions are unchanged afterwards.
- jsdom test: the editor saves `episode` and shows it on reopen.

**Docs impact**: None.

### ORD-003: Play a collection in release order

**Goal**: A block can play its collection by release date, respecting the
precision each date was stored with.

**Scope**:

- Add `release` to `PLAYBACK_MODES` and the editor.
- Compare year, then month, then day. Within a year, year-only dates follow
  dates with a month; within a month, month-only dates follow dates with a
  day. Undated members follow in saved order. Ties by saved position, then
  media item ID.

**Out of scope**: The preview.

**Blocking dependencies**: ORD-002.

**Implementation notes**: Episodes use their own air date, as spec 0001
already stores it. No date is ever invented or parsed beyond its precision.

**Verification**:

- kraziBrain tests for each precision rule, undated members, and ties.
- jsdom test: the editor saves `release`.

**Docs impact**: None.

### ORD-004: Preview the ordered view and upcoming selections

**Goal**: The programming editor shows what the selected order will play
before and after saving.

**Scope**:

- The preview route as decided above, built from the same `ordered-view.ts`
  the scheduler uses.
- Flags: unresolved members, series group boundaries, and duplicate episodes.
- The editor shows the preview for the selected mode and the upcoming
  entries for the saved mode.

**Out of scope**: Reset.

**Blocking dependencies**: ORD-002.

**Implementation notes**: The preview reads; it never generates or writes
entries. Random shows upcoming entries only, since it has no ordered view.

**Verification**:

- Route tests: flags for unresolved, mixed-series, and duplicate members; the
  preview order equals the order the scheduler airs.
- jsdom test: switching the mode select refreshes the preview.

**Docs impact**: None.

### ORD-005: Regenerate when metadata changes an active order

**Goal**: A metadata write that changes an episode or release order
regenerates affected channels after the airing entry, and one that changes no
order does nothing.

**Scope**:

- `order_fingerprint` on ordered progress rows, written by generation.
- The maintenance pass also runs when any block uses `episode` or `release`,
  and regenerates channels whose fingerprint changed with reason
  `ordering_changed`.

**Out of scope**: Collection order and random, which never read metadata.

**Blocking dependencies**: ORD-002.

**Implementation notes**:

- Reuse `CollectionMaintenance`; no writer changes, since every one already
  calls `request()` after commit.
- Read fingerprints and regenerate inside the pass's one `applyInputChange`,
  so the pass never acts on facts older than its transaction.

**Verification**:

- Acceptance tests: a season correction reorders an episode-order channel
  and keeps the airing entry; a title correction leaves the schedule revision
  unchanged; a refresh changing a release date reorders a release-order
  channel; a saved-order channel never regenerates on metadata writes.
- Maintenance test: a pass with no automatic collections still checks
  metadata-ordered blocks.

**Docs impact**: None.

### ORD-006: Reset a channel's progress through a collection

**Goal**: The owner can restart a collection from the beginning in one mode
on one channel, after a warning.

**Scope**:

- The reset route as decided above.
- Ordered modes reset to the beginning; random resets the selection index
  and keeps its seed.
- A **Window dialog** warns that future entries will be regenerated and names
  every block on this channel sharing the collection and mode, then shows the
  upcoming selections.

**Out of scope**: Resetting other collections or modes.

**Blocking dependencies**: ORD-004.

**Implementation notes**: Set `reset_sequence_number` to the first
regenerated entry's sequence number so restoration never returns to
pre-reset progress.

**Verification**:

- Route tests: reset preserves the airing entry, regenerates from the
  beginning for every block sharing the progress, and leaves other
  collections and modes untouched; a later regeneration does not restore
  pre-reset progress.
- jsdom test: the dialog lists shared blocks and cancel changes nothing.

**Docs impact**: Mark the spec `Implemented` when this ticket lands.
